board_content.text: The two roots share the real part $-\tfrac{b}{2a}$ and opposite imaginary parts.
So they are conjugates of each other — a mirror-image pair.
Forgetting $\sqrt{D}=i\sqrt{|D|}$ is the recurring $i^2$ sign-flip error.

segments_english.text: Let's see exactly how the quadratic formula produces complex roots when the discriminant is negative and the coefficients are real.
The only new step is handling the square root of a negative discriminant: write root D as i times root of the size of D.
Concretely, when D is negative, root D equals root of minus the quantity four a c minus b squared, which is i times root of four a c minus b squared.
Substituting into the formula, the roots become minus b plus or minus i root of four a c minus b squared, all over two a.
Look at the structure. Both roots share the same real part, minus b over two a, and they carry opposite imaginary parts because of the plus-or-minus.
So the two roots are conjugates of each other, a mirror-image pair across the real axis, exactly what the discriminant forecast predicted.
The recurring slip here is forgetting that root D equals i times root of the size of D. That's the same i-squared sign-flip error from the very first subtopic, coming back to bite.

A familiar example: x squared plus x plus one equals zero has D equals minus three, giving roots minus one plus or minus i root three, over two — which are exactly omega and omega squared, the cube roots of unity.

segments_hinglish.text: Dekhte hain ki quadratic formula exactly kaise complex roots deta hai jab discriminant negative ho aur coefficients real hon.
Ek hi naya step hai negative discriminant ka square root handle karna: root D ko likho i times root of the size of D.
Concretely, jab D negative hai, root D barabar root of minus the quantity four a c minus b squared, jo hai i times root of four a c minus b squared.
Formula mein substitute karo, to roots ban jaate hain minus b plus or minus i root of four a c minus b squared, poora over two a.
Structure dekho. Dono roots ka same real part hai, minus b over two a, aur unke imaginary parts opposite hain plus-or-minus ki wajah se.
To dono roots ek doosre ke conjugates hain, real axis par ek mirror-image pair, bilkul jaise discriminant forecast ne predict kiya.
Yahan recurring slip hai ye bhoolna ki root D barabar i times root of the size of D. Ye wahi i-squared sign-flip error hai pehle subtopic se, wapas aakar bite karne ke liye.

Ek familiar example: x squared plus x plus one equals zero ka D barabar minus three, deta hai roots minus one plus or minus i root three, over two — jo bilkul omega aur omega squared hain, cube roots of unity.
